title: Tenant Retention Upgrades That Pay Off at Lease Renewal

answer: Tenant retention upgrades are improvements offered at renewal that give a good tenant a reason to stay, such as new flooring in a high-wear room, fresh paint or a bathroom refresh. For commercial tenants, a refreshed suite tied to a longer term does the same job. Every move-out costs vacant days, cleaning, repairs and leasing time.

blocks.x: Keeping a good tenant is often cheaper than finding a new one. Every move-out brings vacant days, cleaning, paint, repairs, marketing and leasing time. The right tenant retention upgrades give that tenant a reason to stay.

In Winnipeg, where more units come under rent regulation in 2027 and the guideline is 3%, turning a regulated unit over just to reset rent has limited upside in a complex of four or more units, because rent for the new tenant is capped at the average of similar units in the complex.

With three units or fewer, the landlord sets the amount, but a vacancy still costs money. That makes renewal upgrades worth a place in a building owner's budget. These rent rules cover residential units only, but a commercial vacancy costs money too.
Why tenant retention upgrades can beat rent discounts

A rent discount lowers your income every month. An upgrade is a one-time cost that stays with the unit and makes it easier to lease next time too. Tenants value improvements they see and use every day.
Residential renewal upgrades
Offer one upgrade with a renewal, chosen from a short menu:
New flooring in a high-wear room
Fresh paint in one or two rooms of their choice
New appliance (dishwasher, microwave, range)
Updated light fixtures or ceiling fans
[Bathroom](/services/bathroom-renovations) refresh: new vanity light, mirror, faucet and fresh caulking
New window coverings, or weatherstripping to cut winter drafts
Letting residents choose makes the offer feel personal.

In a building built or renovated before 1990, check for asbestos before old flooring, plaster or caulking is disturbed, especially with a tenant living in the unit. Our guide covers [asbestos testing before you renovate](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba).
Commercial renewal upgrades
For [office](/services/office-renovations), [retail](/services/retail-renovations) and [medical](/services/medical-dental-office-renovations) tenants, renewal is the moment to negotiate improvements:
**Refresh the suite:** new carpet tile, paint and lighting.
**Reconfigure:** add a meeting room, open up workstations or create a reception area.
**Upgrade washrooms and kitchenettes** in older suites.
**Improve comfort:** fix hot and cold spots, upgrade controls.
Structure it as a [tenant improvement allowance](/blog/tenant-improvement-allowance-winnipeg) tied to a longer renewal term, so the investment pays back over the lease.
How to plan renewal upgrades

**Start about 120 days before lease end.** Manitoba landlords must give a residential fixed-term tenant a renewal at least three months before the agreement ends, so leave time to discuss, price and schedule the work before then.
**Ask what matters to the tenant.** A quick question often reveals an easy win.
**Get firm pricing** before you make the offer, so the numbers work.

**Schedule work around the tenant:** evenings, weekends, or one room at a time. The Residential Tenancies Act limits when a landlord can enter an occupied unit, so get the tenant's agreement on dates and times first.
**Standardize finishes** across your portfolio to control costs and simplify future repairs.
What to track
Renewal rate before and after offering upgrades
Average cost of an upgrade vs. average cost of a turnover
Vacant days per unit per year
Those numbers will tell you whether the program is paying for itself.
The bottom line
Renewal upgrades can keep good tenants, improve your units and avoid the costs of turnover. They're one of the most practical things a building owner can budget for.
